rows.label: c8_bump (default mode; + bump-centre contact detector, receptions as owner events; the frozen submission)
rows.note: verified by a reviewer (197 tests, md5 39562b94a10e23e24c838a1c6c8198ef on two runs at implementation and two at review, on main after the C10, C9 and C11 merges; validator OK; `--mode baseline50` md5 23924df8… unchanged, `--mode m1` d8f4e2a1… and `--mode m2` f394172d… unchanged; `CONTACT_DETECTOR=dv3` through `--config` reproduces c11_restart_chain md5 080ea4f9… exactly, so the detector is the only difference). The largest candidate (RESEARCH-2 rank 1) and the one designed while looking at the public window, so it ran last and under the strictest gate (PLAN 5.1). The ATD ball is smoothed by a symmetric kernel (M13: half-width at half-maximum 11 frames, σ about 9.5, 46 isolated strong peaks over the full match), so a contact is a roughly 24-frame acceleration bump centred on the contact. The old dv_3 detector fired at the start of the speed rise, a median 8 frames early, and could not represent a reception: a ball slowing at a player's feet became a `touch`, which since C7 cannot change the owner. New `events._contact_rows` under `CONTACT_DETECTOR` = `"bump"`: a contact is a local maximum of the vector impulse |v(t+h) − v(t−h)| over ±h frames inside one visible run on alive frames (e_dead ≤ 0.5), stamped at the bump centre, attributed over [c−h, c+h] with R_TOUCH 1.5 m, the 0.4 m contested margin and the existing confidence rule. Kind from the signed speed change against `REDIRECT_FRACTION` × |J|: a kick is a `release`; a receive is a `control` (note `receive`, an owner event under release_or_control); a redirect by the owning team is a `touch`; a redirect by the other team is a `control` only if that team's next uncontested contact or slow-ball control run is also theirs with no dead frame between (Metrica's "no significant impact" clause), else no row. Slow-ball control runs, dribble rows and the decoder are unchanged. `--mode m2` forces `"dv3"` through `possession.dv3_config`, so the old rows stay reproducible; one event table feeds both the owner walk and the dead-ball module, and giving dead ball the old rows is byte-identical. No airborne filter on bump contacts (as the prototype). Config `CONTACT_HALF_WINDOW` = 12 (M13: 11 + 1), `DV_CONTACT` = 9.0 m/s, `REDIRECT_FRACTION` = 0.5; hash 4289ca40cf → e76f95ffb0; 12 new synthetic tests on Gaussian-smoothed tracks (σ 9.5), 185 → 197, the P1-A tests pinned to `"dv3"`. No debugging iterations: the first build reproduced the prototype's public pattern. `DV_CONTACT` comes from a pre-stated rule, not from the score: the loosest 1 m/s step giving at most 3.0 H↔A switches per alive minute on the full match, measured on the engine that ships. On the C10 base the band said 11 (rates at DV 7..13: 3.55, 3.40, 3.18, 3.07, 2.88, 2.75, 2.73). On the merged engine, where C9 removes switches near the goalkeeper swaps, it says 9 (3.20, 3.05, 2.86, 2.75, 2.61, 2.48, 2.45). The rate line is flat from DV 8 to 11, so DV is weakly determined. The DV 11 variant on the merged engine: md5 12d16c33…, public 0.747, 237 possessions, 12/8/4 @25, leave-one-out 19 of 20 with one tie. Public: spellF1 0.680 → 0.750, macroF1 0.914 → 0.948, 13/7/5 @25 (was 11/9/5), mean latency −2.5 → −2.6, spells matched at IoU 0.3 to 0.7 11/11/11/9/9 → 13/13/13/12/9; same as the research composite prototype (0.750, 13/7/5). Gained 11624 (missed → −1) and 14846 (missed → −9), lost none; 13704 −7 → 0, 15346 +9 → +13, 17293 +11 → +3; unchanged 12851 0, 12989 0, 15889 −10, 16400 +5, 17380 −9, 17838 −2, 18027 −2, 18389 −22; missed by both 11351, 11553, 12665, 13785, 15365, 15766, 15799; spurious c11 11501, 12710, 14010, 14882, 15471 → c8 11501, 11580, 12623, 13831, 15428.
